title: Benchmark environment capture
description: The environment.json sealed into every evidence bundle: source, toolchain, host, and broker identity at attempt time. Written by crates/benchctl/src/environment.rs, a Rust port of the legacy capture with "unavailable" fallbacks. Supersedes kafkars.benchmark-environment.v1 by making source a repo-agnostic map instead of three hardcoded repository keys. Identity is the sha256 of the canonical bytes with captured_at removed, the same rule as v1. Documentation mirror of the EnvironmentDocument serde type in crates/bench-schema/src/environment.rs, which is the source of truth.

captured_at.description: UTC RFC 3339 capture instant. Excluded from the environment identity hash.

source.description: Git state per repository, keyed by repository name. Repo-agnostic: a benchmark of any client records whichever repositories it depends on. A missing checkout still records an entry so provenance degrades gracefully.

commit.description: Commit hash, or "unavailable" when the checkout is missing.

dirty.description: True when the worktree has uncommitted changes; a dirty bundle is never claim-eligible.

toolchain.description: Compiler and runtime versions. Any unavailable command records the literal string "unavailable".

host.description: Host identity, read from sysctl on Darwin and /proc on Linux.

broker.description: Broker identity. The cluster lifecycle is always owned by the caller, never by benchctl.
